extra_vocab.en: a metal object that pulls iron toward it
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡指用來取代彈簧、控制鎖定與解鎖的零件。文章中的 two magnets 是兩個磁鐵靠磁力互相作用。

example.en: Both magnets must be tested before the product leaves the factory.
example.zh: 兩個磁鐵都必須在產品出廠前測試。

example.en: A permanent magnet keeps its force without any electric power.
example.zh: 永久磁鐵不需要任何電力就能保有磁力。

example.en: A strong magnet can damage some credit cards and watches.
example.zh: 強力磁鐵可能損壞某些信用卡和手錶。

example.en: Please attach a magnet to the end of the pin.
example.zh: 請在銷的末端裝上一個磁鐵。

examples.en: We tested a small magnet to hold the cover in place.
examples.zh: 我們測試了一個小磁鐵來固定外蓋。

examples.en: The magnet in this latch is strong enough to hold the door.
examples.zh: 這個門扣裡的磁鐵強到足以固定住門。

examples.en: The new shopping center became a magnet for young families.
examples.zh: 這間新購物中心成了吸引年輕家庭的地方。

confusable.diff: magnitude 是「大小、規模」，拼法和 magnet 很像，但和磁鐵無關。

example.en: The magnitude of the price change surprised the whole sales team.
example.zh: 價格變動的幅度讓整個業務團隊很驚訝。

example.en: The pin is made of metal, not plastic.
example.zh: 這個銷是金屬做的，不是塑膠。

example.en: The spring pushes the button back after each use.
example.zh: 每次使用後，彈簧會把按鈕推回原位。

example.en: The force of the magnet depends on its size.
example.zh: 磁鐵的力量取決於它的大小。

senses.en: a metal object that pulls iron toward it

example.en: The two magnets move the locking pin without touching it.
example.zh: 這兩個磁鐵不用碰到鎖定銷就能讓它移動。

senses.en: a person or place that attracts many people
senses.distinguish: 後面常接 for 或 to，指地點、公司等，不是真的磁鐵。

example.en: Our city is a magnet for international investors.
example.zh: 我們的城市對國際投資人很有吸引力。

extra_vocab.en: to pull something toward you or make people want to come
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡是物理上的「互相吸引」：兩個磁鐵的磁力讓它們靠近，和 repel（互相排斥）成對使用。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: attract 是及物動詞，後面直接接受詞，不加 to；「被…吸引」要用被動 be attracted to。

example.en: This design attracts buyers because it is simple and light.
example.zh: 這個設計吸引買家，因為它簡單又輕巧。

example.en: The trade show attracted over five hundred visitors last year.
example.zh: 這場展覽去年吸引了超過五百位參觀者。

example.en: We are attracting more clients through our new website.
example.zh: 我們正透過新網站吸引更多客戶。

example.en: Free samples can attract new customers to our booth.
example.zh: 免費試用品可以吸引新顧客來到我們的攤位。

example.en: The bright sign will attract attention from people walking by.
example.zh: 這個亮眼的招牌會吸引路過的人注意。

example.en: A clear business plan will help us attract more investors.
example.zh: 清楚的商業計畫會幫助我們吸引更多投資人。

examples.en: Opposite poles attract each other, while the same poles repel.
examples.zh: 異極互相吸引，同極則互相排斥。

examples.en: The festival attracts thousands of visitors every year.
examples.zh: 這個節慶每年吸引數千名遊客。

examples.en: The company offers good benefits to attract skilled workers.
examples.zh: 公司提供良好福利來吸引技術人員。

confusable.diff: distract 是「使分心」，和 attract 只差開頭，意思完全不同。

example.en: Loud noise in the office can distract workers from their tasks.
example.zh: 辦公室的大聲噪音會讓員工無法專心工作。

confusable.diff: extract 是「取出、萃取」，指把東西從裡面拿出來。
confusable.usage: extract 常接 from：extract data from the system。

example.en: We extract the data from the system every Monday morning.
example.zh: 我們每週一早上從系統取出資料。

similar.diff: draw 比較口語，常接 in 或 to，語氣和 attract 相近但更簡單。

example.en: The sale is meant to draw more shoppers into the store.
example.zh: 這次特賣是為了把更多顧客吸引進店裡。

similar.diff: appeal to 是「對…有吸引力」，主詞是東西，後面接人。

example.en: Our new model will appeal to younger drivers.
example.zh: 我們的新車款會吸引年輕駕駛。

example.en: The new store draws many shoppers on weekends.
example.zh: 這間新店在週末吸引許多顧客。

example.en: The new product design interested several large retailers last month.
example.zh: 這個新產品設計上個月引起幾家大型零售商的興趣。

example.en: The magnet can pull the pin back quickly.
example.zh: 磁鐵可以很快把銷拉回來。

senses.en: to pull something closer by a natural force

example.en: Magnets attract small pieces of iron but not plastic.
example.zh: 磁鐵會吸引小塊的鐵，但不會吸引塑膠。

senses.en: to make people interested or make them come
senses.distinguish: 主詞是產品、地點或做法，受詞是人或資金，不是物理拉力。

example.en: Good service attracts customers who return again and again.
example.zh: 好的服務會吸引顧客一再回來。

extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡指兩個磁鐵因磁力互相推開，和 attract 成對出現，說明磁鐵如何讓鎖定銷來回移動。

example.en: This cover repels dust and makes cleaning much easier.
example.zh: 這個外蓋能防塵，讓清潔容易許多。

example.en: The new coating repelled water during all of our tests.
example.zh: 新的塗層在我們所有測試中都能防水。

example.en: Slow delivery is repelling customers from our online store.
example.zh: 遲緩的送貨正讓顧客遠離我們的網路商店。

example.en: If you turn one magnet around, the two will repel each other.
example.zh: 如果你把一個磁鐵轉過來，兩個就會互相排斥。

example.en: This lamp is designed to repel insects in the evening.
example.zh: 這盞燈是設計來在傍晚驅趕蚊蟲的。

examples.en: This coating helps repel water and keeps the fabric dry.
examples.zh: 這個塗層能防水，讓布料保持乾燥。

examples.en: Engineers use this force to repel parts from each other.
examples.zh: 工程師利用這種力量讓零件互相推開。

examples.en: Aggressive sales tactics can repel customers rather than win them over.
examples.zh: 強勢的銷售手法可能讓顧客反感，而不是爭取到他們。

confusable.diff: repeal 是「廢除（法律、規定）」，拼法只差一個字母，和排斥無關。

example.en: The government voted to repeal the old trade rule.
example.zh: 政府投票廢除了舊的貿易規定。

confusable.diff: expel 是「開除、逐出」，指把人趕出組織或學校。
confusable.usage: expel 的對象通常是人，常接 from：expel someone from a group。

example.en: The company may expel members who break the rules.
example.zh: 公司可能會把違反規定的成員除名。

similar.diff: push away 是口語說法，指用力推開；repel 較正式，也用於磁力與防水。

example.en: The pole of one magnet will push away the other.
example.zh: 一個磁鐵的磁極會把另一個推開。

similar.diff: drive away 常用在把人或顧客「趕跑」，語氣比 repel 更強。

example.en: Poor service may drive away our most loyal customers.
example.zh: 糟糕的服務可能趕走我們最忠實的顧客。

example.en: The committee decided to reject the first design.
example.zh: 委員會決定否決第一版設計。

example.en: The new material can resist heat and water.
example.zh: 這種新材料能耐熱也耐水。

example.en: Push this button to release the lock on the door.
example.zh: 按下這個按鈕來解開門上的鎖。

derived.link: repel + -ent，變成「有排斥作用的（東西）」，像 different、student

senses.en: to push away from each other, like two magnets

example.en: Magnets repel each other when their matching poles meet.
example.zh: 磁鐵的相同磁極相遇時會互相排斥。

senses.en: to keep water, insects or dirt away
senses.distinguish: 受詞是水、蟲、灰塵等，常見於產品說明。

example.en: A special oil on the bag helps repel rain.
example.zh: 袋子上的特殊油層有助於防雨。

senses.en: to make people feel they do not want to come close
senses.distinguish: 受詞是人，常用來描述態度或做法讓人不想靠近。

example.en: His rude emails repelled several of our best clients.
example.zh: 他無禮的電子郵件讓我們幾位最好的客戶反感。

extra_vocab.en: the way parts or things are put in order
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡指零件的機械「配置」，a different mechanical arrangement 是用不同的零件排列方式達到相同功能。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 表示「安排、準備」時常用複數 arrangements，後面接 for + 名詞或 to + V，例如 make arrangements for the trip。

example.en: Final arrangements for the product launch will be sent by email.
example.zh: 產品發表的最終安排會用電子郵件寄出。

example.en: Please make arrangements for the client's hotel stay.
example.zh: 請為客戶的飯店住宿做好安排。

example.en: Our assistant will handle all travel arrangements for the trip.
example.zh: 我們的助理會處理這趟行程所有的旅行安排。

example.en: The seating arrangement for the dinner has been changed.
example.zh: 晚宴的座位安排已經更改了。

examples.en: This arrangement of parts reduces the size of the lock.
examples.zh: 這種零件配置縮小了鎖的尺寸。

examples.en: The two companies reached a flexible payment arrangement last week.
examples.zh: 兩家公司上週達成了彈性的付款安排。

examples.en: The arrangement of the buttons makes the device easy to use.
examples.zh: 按鈕的排列方式讓這個裝置很好操作。

confusable.diff: agreement 是「協議、同意」，指雙方談好的內容；arrangement 偏重「安排、配置」。

example.en: Both sides signed the agreement before the end of the month.
example.zh: 雙方在月底前簽署了協議。

similar.diff: layout 指空間或頁面的「版面配置」，arrangement 範圍更廣，也可指安排。

example.en: The layout of the new office is open and bright.
example.zh: 新辦公室的配置開放又明亮。

similar.diff: setup 指設備或系統的「設置、組態」，語氣較口語。

example.en: The setup of the machine takes about ten minutes.
example.zh: 這台機器的設置大約要十分鐘。

example.en: We need a clear plan before the project starts.
example.zh: 專案開始前我們需要一個清楚的計畫。

example.en: The design of the lock is simple and safe.
example.zh: 這個鎖的設計簡單又安全。

example.en: The structure of the lock has only three parts.
example.zh: 這個鎖的結構只有三個零件。

derived.link: 動詞詞幹，加 -ment 變名詞 arrangement，像 pay → payment

senses.en: the way parts or things are placed together

example.en: The arrangement of the gears lets the machine run quietly.
example.zh: 齒輪的配置讓機器運轉得很安靜。

senses.en: a plan made in advance for something to happen
senses.distinguish: 通常用複數，後面接 for 活動或行程，指事前的準備。

example.en: All arrangements for the meeting were finished on Friday.
example.zh: 會議的所有安排在星期五都已完成。

senses.en: an agreement between people or companies
senses.distinguish: 前面常有 under this 或 payment、work 等字，指雙方談定的做法。

example.en: Under this arrangement, we deliver goods every two weeks.
example.zh: 依照這項約定，我們每兩週送一次貨。

extra_vocab.en: a basic idea about how something works
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡指機構運作的基本原理，the basic principle 就是前面說明的「用磁力控制鎖定銷」這個核心概念。

example.en: These three principles guide every decision our team makes.
example.zh: 這三項原則指引我們團隊的每個決定。

example.en: Please explain the basic principle of this new system.
example.zh: 請說明這個新系統的基本原理。

example.en: In principle, the plan is fine, but we need more details.
example.zh: 原則上這個計畫可行，但我們需要更多細節。

example.en: Safety is our guiding principle in every product design.
example.zh: 安全是我們每項產品設計的指導原則。

examples.en: Both machines work on the same basic principle.
examples.zh: 這兩台機器的運作基於相同的基本原理。

examples.en: Honesty is an important principle for everyone in our company.
examples.zh: 誠實是我們公司每個人都重視的原則。

examples.en: Customer trust is the main principle behind our service.
examples.zh: 客戶信任是我們服務背後的主要原則。

confusable.diff: principal 發音和 principle 完全一樣，意思是「主要的」或「校長」。
confusable.usage: principle 是名詞（原理、原則）；principal 多為形容詞「主要的」，也可當名詞「校長」。

example.en: Our principal supplier is located near the main factory.
example.zh: 我們的主要供應商就在主工廠附近。

similar.diff: rule 是明確規定、要遵守的「規則」；principle 是背後的基本想法。

example.en: Every employee must follow the safety rule at all times.
example.zh: 每位員工都必須隨時遵守安全規則。

similar.diff: concept 是「概念」，偏重想法本身；principle 偏重運作的原理。

example.en: The basic concept is easy to explain to new staff.
example.zh: 這個基本概念很容易向新進員工說明。

example.en: The theory sounds good, but we must test it first.
example.zh: 這個理論聽起來不錯，但我們必須先測試。

example.en: Our refund policy is explained clearly on the website.
example.zh: 我們的退款政策在網站上有清楚說明。

example.en: This product meets the highest safety standard in the industry.
example.zh: 這個產品符合業界最高的安全標準。

senses.en: a basic idea about how something works

example.en: The principle of this heater is simple and safe.
example.zh: 這台暖氣機的原理簡單又安全。

senses.en: a rule or belief about what is right
senses.distinguish: 指人或公司遵守的信念，常見 as a matter of principle。

example.en: As a matter of principle, we never share customer data.
example.zh: 基於原則，我們絕不分享客戶資料。

extra_vocab.en: a small metal part that holds something in a fixed position
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡是鎖定機構中的關鍵零件：傳統設計用纜線拉動、彈簧推回；新設計改由磁鐵控制它前後移動。
extra_vocab.pattern: locking + N（具鎖定功能的零件）
extra_vocab.grammar_note: locking 是 V-ing 當形容詞，表示「用來鎖定的」；locked pin 則是「被鎖住的銷」，兩者意思不同。

examples.en: The locking pin holds the seat in position while the car moves.
examples.zh: 鎖定銷在車子行進時把座椅固定在位置上。

examples.en: Remove the locking pin before you replace the old part.
examples.zh: 更換舊零件前，請先取下鎖定銷。

examples.en: Check that the locking pin is fully inserted into the hole.
examples.zh: 請確認鎖定銷已完全插入孔中。

examples.en: The inspector found a damaged locking pin on the third machine.
examples.zh: 檢驗員在第三台機器上發現一根受損的鎖定銷。

similar.diff: lock pin 是較簡短的說法，意思幾乎相同，locking pin 比較常見於技術說明。

example.en: Insert the lock pin into the hole to fix the panel.
example.zh: 把鎖銷插入孔中來固定面板。

similar.diff: latch 是「門閂、扣鎖」，是整個扣住的裝置；locking pin 則是裡面的一根銷。

example.en: Close the latch so the cover stays shut during transport.
example.zh: 請扣上門扣，讓外蓋在運送時保持關閉。
